    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Authentication failures are swallowed, allowing protected handlers to run",
    "description": "The require_auth decorator catches the 401 exception raised by abort(), clears g.user, and still invokes the protected handler. As a result, endpoints intended to require authentication can disclose data or fail with an unrelated server error instead of rejecting the request.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/auth.py:51-58 catches every exception and returns f(*args, **kwargs). GET /orders/1 without an Authorization header returned HTTP 200 with the complete order contents; GET /account without authentication proceeded to a 500 response."
  },
  {

    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Order details do not verify ownership",
    "description": "show_order retrieves an order with get_order() rather than own_order(), so it never compares customer_id with the authenticated user. A requester who reaches the endpoint can read another customer's order contents, payment amounts, refunds, and delivery information.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/orders.py:46-49 calls order_json(get_order(order_id)) without an ownership check. GET /orders/1 without authentication returned HTTP 200 and the full order JSON because the authentication decorator also fails open."
  },

    "title": "Trailing-slash refund route bypasses the staff authorization check",
    "description": "Global admin authorization compares request.path to exact registered rules. The refund route accepts both slash forms with strict_slashes=False, but the trailing-slash path is not equal to the registered rule and the handler has no local authorization check. Unauthenticated users can therefore create goodwill refunds.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/__init__.py:26-41 performs the exact path comparison; shopapi/admin.py:51-53 registers /admin/refunds with strict_slashes=False. POST /admin/refunds/ without credentials and {\"order_id\":1,\"amount_pence\":1} returned HTTP 200 with {\"ok\":true} and created a refund."

  },

    "title": "Unsigned basket cookie is deserialized with pickle",
    "description": "The basket cookie is entirely client-controlled and is passed to pickle.loads without an integrity check. A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python code in the application process whenever a basket endpoint reads it.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/basket.py:15-23 base64-decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads; shopapi/basket.py:26-28 creates the cookie without signing it. The exception handler only handles errors after deserialization and does not prevent pickle gadget execution."
  },
